# Automatic shape text color

Original OOXML fixture, generated by `tools/shape_auto_color_fixture.py` using
python-docx (MIT), lxml (BSD), and the Python standard library. No user template
or font files are redistributed. The reference application produced the native PDF.
`tools/shape_auto_color_reference.py` records source/PDF hashes, native text RGB
and glyph crops. Regenerate the PDF with `tools/export-reference.ps1`.

The 36 cases cross white/black/green fills with white/red fontRef colors and
omitted, paragraph-style automatic, character-style automatic, direct automatic,
and explicit blue text. Six additional cases omit fontRef and compare automatic
with explicit blue. Automatic text follows fontRef regardless of fill; without
fontRef it contrasts with the solid fill. Explicit blue always remains blue.

ECMA-376 Part 1 17.3.2.6 describes consumer-chosen automatic color based on the
background; 20.1.4.1.17 supplies the font reference and color. The controls flag
the reference application's interoperability behavior: a fontRef color takes precedence over that
background-based automatic choice, even white on white. This is independent of
whether auto is declared in paragraph, character, or direct run formatting.

Browser checks compare strong colored glyph pixels against antialiased glyph
coverage in both directions within two pixels. A same-color foreground/fill
case instead requires the crop to stay uniformly that color. Initial per-pixel
shade comparisons exposed native/browser glyph antialiasing differences; case
5 was visually inspected at enlarged scale before choosing coverage masks.
Body edits, exact no-edit/undo exports, untouched parts and reopened rendering
are checked. Transparent, gradient, pattern and picture fill contrast without
fontRef is not established by this fixture and retains the prior behavior.
